 210: def test_real_bedrock_tool_use_round_trip():
 211:     """Real Haiku-4.5 round-trip: send "list files in CURRENT_DIR",
 212:     assert tool_use(name="list_dir") is in the response â†’ run the tool
 213:     locally â†’ send tool_result â†’ assert final text mentions the listing.
 214:     ~$0.005 per call.
 215: 
 216:     Validates the full Bedrock tool-use loop end-to-end:
 217:     1. We send the tool schema list_dir + a user message.
 218:     2. Bedrock returns a tool_use block.
 219:     3. We execute list_dir locally.
 220:     4. We send tool_result back.
 221:     5. Bedrock returns a final text answer.
 222:     """

 225:     from tools.registry import _reset_registry_for_tests
 226:     from tools import bootstrap_built_ins, find_tool_by_name, all_registered

 234:     region = os.getenv("AWS_REGION", "ap-southeast-2")
 235:     client = BedrockClient(model_id=_HAIKU_45_MODEL_ID, region=region, mock_mode=False)
 236:

 238:         "name": "list_dir",
 239:         "description": list_dir_tool.description,
 240:         "input_schema": list_dir_tool.input_schema,
 241:     }]
 242: 
 243:     # Round-trip 1: user asks, model returns tool_use.
 244:     messages = [{
 245:         "role": "user",
 246:         "content": "List the files in the current directory using the list_dir tool, then summarize.",
 247:     }]
 248:     response = client.chat(
 249:         messages=messages,
 250:         system="You are a helpful assistant. Use the list_dir tool when asked to list files.",
 251:         tools=tool_schema,
 252:         max_tokens=512,

 270:                 "type": "tool_use",

  32: def _load_agent_status_text() -> Optional[str]:
  33:     """Return the contents of `<workspace>/AGENT_STATUS.md`, or None.
  34: 
  35:     Honors CONFIG.enable_status_doc + CONFIG.status_doc + CONFIG.workspace.
  36:     Returns None silently when the file is missing or disabled â€” the
  37:     handoff path is a v4 capability that gracefully degrades.
  38:     """

  40:     from runtime.config import CONFIG
  41:     if not getattr(CONFIG, "enable_status_doc", True):

  44:     if not os.path.isfile(status_path):
  45:         return None

  50:         return None

  70:         system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
  71:         plan_mode: bool = False,

  75:         """Construct the Agent.
  76: 
  77:         Args:
  78:             client: BedrockClient (or mock with the same `chat(...)` shape).
  79:             max_turns: hard upper bound on turns per `run()` call.
  80:             budget: shared IterationBudget. If None, a fresh one is created.
  81:             skill_manager: optional SkillManager for active-skill prompt
  82:                 injection + auto-trigger reminder (Phase 10 wiring).
  83:             on_stop_check: callable returning True if user pressed Stop.
  84:             system_prompt: override the default `prompt.build_system_prompt`.
  85:                 If None, the static v5 prompt is used.
  86:             plan_mode: when True, the dispatch gate enforces the v4
  87:                 PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS read-only allowlist.
  88:             thinking_enabled: send thinking config on every Bedrock call.
  89:             thinking_budget: max tokens for thinking (PS Issue #4 surfaces this).
  90:         """
  91:         self.client = client
  92:         self.budget = budget if budget is not None else IterationBudget()
  93:         self.skill_manager = skill_manager
  94:         self._stop_requested = False
  95: 
  96:         def _combined_stop():
  97:             if self._stop_requested:
  98:                 return True
  99:             if on_stop_check is not None and on_stop_check():
 100:                 return True
 101:             return False
 102: 
 103:         self._engine = QueryEngine(
 104:             client=client,
 105:             max_turns=max_turns,
 106:             budget=self.budget,
 107:             on_stop_check=_combined_stop,
 108:             skill_manager=skill_manager,
 109:         )
 110:         self._system_prompt = system_prompt
 111:         self._plan_mode = bool(plan_mode)
 112:         self._thinking_enabled = bool(thinking_enabled)
 113:         self._thinking_budget = int(thinking_budget)
 114:         # Block B+: AGENT_STATUS auto-load runs once on the first run() call.
 115:         self._agent_status_loaded = False
 116:         self._agent_status_text: Optional[str] = None

 118:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
 119:     # Public surface
 120:     # ------------------------------------------------------------
 121: 
 122:     def run(
 123:         self,
 124:         message: str,
 125:         tools: Optional[List[Any]] = None,
 126:         output_fn: Callable[[str], None] = print,
 127:     ) -> QueryResult:
 128:         """Execute a single user turn. Returns the `QueryResult`."""
 129:         # Lazy-import to avoid circular import on package init
 130:         from prompt import build_system_prompt, CACHE_BOUNDARY
 131:         from tools import all_registered
 132: 
 133:         # Block B+: AGENT_STATUS auto-load on first run() call. Reads
 134:         # `<workspace>/AGENT_STATUS.md` (or CONFIG.status_doc) and
 135:         # appends it to the dynamic tail of the system prompt so the
 136:         # agent picks up handoff context from a previous session.
 137:         # Reads file ONCE per Agent instance (idempotent).
 138:         if not self._agent_status_loaded and self._system_prompt is None:
 139:             try:
 140:                 self._agent_status_text = _load_agent_status_text()
 141:             except Exception:
 142:                 self._agent_status_text = None
 143:             self._agent_status_loaded = True
 144: 
 145:         system_prompt = self._system_prompt or build_system_prompt(ctx={})
 146:         if self._agent_status_text:
 147:             # Append to the dynamic tail (after CACHE_BOUNDARY) so the
 148:             # cache-aware prefix replay (Block G2 territory) still works.
 149:             if CACHE_BOUNDARY in system_prompt:
 150:                 system_prompt = (
 151:                     system_prompt + "\n\n## Handoff: AGENT_STATUS\n\n"
 152:                     + self._agent_status_text
 153:                 )
 154:             else:
 155:                 system_prompt = (
 156:                     system_prompt + CACHE_BOUNDARY
 157:                     + "\n\n## Handoff: AGENT_STATUS\n\n"
 158:                     + self._agent_status_text
 159:                 )
 160:         active_tools = list(tools) if tools is not None else all_registered()
 161: 
 162:         self._stop_requested = False  # reset between runs
 163:         result = self._engine.run(
 164:             user_message=message,
 165:             system_prompt=system_prompt,
 166:             tools=active_tools,
 167:             plan_mode=self._plan_mode,
 168:             output_fn=output_fn,
 169:             thinking_enabled=self._thinking_enabled,
 170:             thinking_budget=self._thinking_budget,
 171:         )
 172:         return result
 173: 
 174:     def stop(self) -> None:
 175:         """Request the next-turn checkpoint to break out of the loop."""
 176:         self._stop_requested = True
 177: 
 178:     def clear(self, reset_budget: bool = False) -> None:
 179:         """Reset the conversation buffer. Optionally also reset the budget.
 180: 
 181:         By default the budget is preserved across `clear()` so a user who
 182:         wants a fresh conversation but still respects the cost ceiling

+"""V5 agent.py — public Agent class (Phase 11, ADR-017).
+
+Thin wrapper that composes the Phase 1-10 surfaces:
+  - `runtime.bedrock_client.BedrockClient` (Phase 1)
+  - `core.budget.IterationBudget` (Phase 8)
+  - `core.query_engine.QueryEngine` (Phase 8)
+  - optional `skills.manager.SkillManager` (Phase 10)
+
+Public methods:
+  - `run(message)` — execute a single user turn, return a `QueryResult`.
+  - `stop()` — request the next turn to halt cleanly.
+  - `clear()` — reset conversation buffer (does NOT reset budget by default;
+                callers can pass `reset_budget=True` to also reset the budget).
+
+This is the surface chat.ipynb (Phase 11) drives. It does NOT re-implement
+agent logic — every behavior lives in its own module (Phase 8-10).
+
+PORT_LOG: #031.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, List, Optional
+
+from core import IterationBudget, QueryEngine
+from core.query_engine import QueryResult
+
+
+# ============================================================
+# Block B+ helper — load AGENT_STATUS.md if present
+# ============================================================
+
+def _load_agent_status_text() -> Optional[str]:
+    """Return the contents of `<workspace>/AGENT_STATUS.md`, or None.
+
+    Honors CONFIG.enable_status_doc + CONFIG.status_doc + CONFIG.workspace.
+    Returns None silently when the file is missing or disabled — the
+    handoff path is a v4 capability that gracefully degrades.
+    """
+    import os
+    from runtime.config import CONFIG
+    if not getattr(CONFIG, "enable_status_doc", True):
+        return None
+    status_path = os.path.join(CONFIG.workspace, CONFIG.status_doc)
+    if not os.path.isfile(status_path):
+        return None
+    try:
+        with open(status_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            text = f.read()
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    text = text.strip()
+    if not text:
+        return None
+    # Cap at ~8 KB so a runaway status doc can't blow out the prompt.
+    if len(text) > 8000:
+        text = text[:8000] + "\n\n…[truncated; AGENT_STATUS.md exceeds 8 KB]"
+    return text
+
+
+class Agent:
+    """Minimal public Agent wrapping the Phase 8-10 surfaces."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        client: Any,
+        max_turns: int = 50,
+        budget: Optional[IterationBudget] = None,
+        skill_manager: Optional[Any] = None,
+        on_stop_check: Optional[Callable[[], bool]] = None,
+        system_prompt: Optional[str] = None,
+        plan_mode: bool = False,
+        thinking_enabled: bool = False,
+        thinking_budget: int = 4096,
+    ):
+        """Construct the Agent.
+
+        Args:
+            client: BedrockClient (or mock with the same `chat(...)` shape).
+            max_turns: hard upper bound on turns per `run()` call.
+            budget: shared IterationBudget. If None, a fresh one is created.
+            skill_manager: optional SkillManager for active-skill prompt
+                injection + auto-trigger reminder (Phase 10 wiring).
+            on_stop_check: callable returning True if user pressed Stop.
+            system_prompt: override the default `prompt.build_system_prompt`.
+                If None, the static v5 prompt is used.
+            plan_mode: when True, the dispatch gate enforces the v4
+                PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS read-only allowlist.
+            thinking_enabled: send thinking config on every Bedrock call.
+            thinking_budget: max tokens for thinking (PS Issue #4 surfaces this).
+        """
+        self.client = client
+        self.budget = budget if budget is not None else IterationBudget()
+        self.skill_manager = skill_manager
+        self._stop_requested = False
+
+        def _combined_stop():
+            if self._stop_requested:
+                return True
+            if on_stop_check is not None and on_stop_check():
+                return True
+            return False
+
+        self._engine = QueryEngine(
+            client=client,
+            max_turns=max_turns,
+            budget=self.budget,
+            on_stop_check=_combined_stop,
+            skill_manager=skill_manager,
+        )
+        self._system_prompt = system_prompt
+        self._plan_mode = bool(plan_mode)
+        self._thinking_enabled = bool(thinking_enabled)
+        self._thinking_budget = int(thinking_budget)
+        # Block B+: AGENT_STATUS auto-load runs once on the first run() call.
+        self._agent_status_loaded = False
+        self._agent_status_text: Optional[str] = None
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Public surface
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def run(
+        self,
+        message: str,
+        tools: Optional[List[Any]] = None,
+        output_fn: Callable[[str], None] = print,
+    ) -> QueryResult:
+        """Execute a single user turn. Returns the `QueryResult`."""
+        # Lazy-import to avoid circular import on package init
+        from prompt import build_system_prompt, CACHE_BOUNDARY
+        from tools import all_registered
+
+        # Block B+: AGENT_STATUS auto-load on first run() call. Reads
+        # `<workspace>/AGENT_STATUS.md` (or CONFIG.status_doc) and
+        # appends it to the dynamic tail of the system prompt so the
+        # agent picks up handoff context from a previous session.
+        # Reads file ONCE per Agent instance (idempotent).
+        if not self._agent_status_loaded and self._system_prompt is None:
+            try:
+                self._agent_status_text = _load_agent_status_text()
+            except Exception:
+                self._agent_status_text = None
+            self._agent_status_loaded = True
+
+        system_prompt = self._system_prompt or build_system_prompt(ctx={})
+        if self._agent_status_text:
+            # Append to the dynamic tail (after CACHE_BOUNDARY) so the
+            # cache-aware prefix replay (Block G2 territory) still works.
+            if CACHE_BOUNDARY in system_prompt:
+                system_prompt = (
+                    system_prompt + "\n\n## Handoff: AGENT_STATUS\n\n"
+                    + self._agent_status_text
+                )
+            else:
+                system_prompt = (
+                    system_prompt + CACHE_BOUNDARY
+                    + "\n\n## Handoff: AGENT_STATUS\n\n"
+                    + self._agent_status_text
+                )
+        active_tools = list(tools) if tools is not None else all_registered()
+
+        self._stop_requested = False  # reset between runs
+        result = self._engine.run(
+            user_message=message,
+            system_prompt=system_prompt,
+            tools=active_tools,
+            plan_mode=self._plan_mode,
+            output_fn=output_fn,
+            thinking_enabled=self._thinking_enabled,
+            thinking_budget=self._thinking_budget,
+        )
+        return result
+
+    def stop(self) -> None:
+        """Request the next-turn checkpoint to break out of the loop."""
+        self._stop_requested = True
+
+    def clear(self, reset_budget: bool = False) -> None:
+        """Reset the conversation buffer. Optionally also reset the budget.
+
+        By default the budget is preserved across `clear()` so a user who
+        wants a fresh conversation but still respects the cost ceiling
+        doesn't have to pass anything special. Pass `reset_budget=True`
+        for the more aggressive reset.
+        """
+        self._engine.messages = []
+        self._engine._discovered_tool_names = set()
+        if reset_budget:
+            self.budget.reset()
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Read-only views (used by Phase 11 widgets)
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    @property
+    def messages(self) -> list:
+        """Snapshot of the conversation buffer (for the chat UI to render)."""
+        return list(self._engine.messages)
+
+    @property
+    def thinking_enabled(self) -> bool:
+        return self._thinking_enabled
+
+    @property
+    def thinking_budget(self) -> int:
+        return self._thinking_budget
+
+    def set_thinking(self, enabled: bool, budget: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
+        """Update thinking-mode settings (PS Issue #4 UI hook)."""
+        self._thinking_enabled = bool(enabled)
+        if budget is not None:
+            self._thinking_budget = int(budget)

+def test_zip_rebuild_succeeds():
+    """`python _rebuild_zip.py` produces compact_v5.zip without errors."""
+    assert _REBUILD_SCRIPT.is_file(), f"missing rebuild script: {_REBUILD_SCRIPT}"
+    result = subprocess.run(

+        text=True,
+        timeout=60,
+    )
+    assert result.returncode == 0, (
+        f"_rebuild_zip.py failed (rc={result.returncode}):\n"
+        f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout}\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr}"
+    )
+    assert _SHIP_ZIP.is_file(), f"compact_v5.zip not produced at {_SHIP_ZIP}"
+    # Sanity-check: zip is non-trivial.
+    assert _SHIP_ZIP.stat().st_size > 50_000, (
+        f"compact_v5.zip suspiciously small: {_SHIP_ZIP.stat().st_size} bytes"
+    )

+def test_real_bedrock_tool_use_round_trip():
+    """Real Haiku-4.5 round-trip: send "list files in CURRENT_DIR",
+    assert tool_use(name="list_dir") is in the response → run the tool
+    locally → send tool_result → assert final text mentions the listing.
+    ~$0.005 per call.
+
+    Validates the full Bedrock tool-use loop end-to-end:
+    1. We send the tool schema list_dir + a user message.
+    2. Bedrock returns a tool_use block.
+    3. We execute list_dir locally.
+    4. We send tool_result back.
+    5. Bedrock returns a final text answer.
+    """
+    _require_real_bedrock()
+    from runtime.bedrock_client import BedrockClient
+    from tools.registry import _reset_registry_for_tests
+    from tools import bootstrap_built_ins, find_tool_by_name, all_registered
+
+    _reset_registry_for_tests()
+    bootstrap_built_ins()
+
+    list_dir_tool = find_tool_by_name(all_registered(), "list_dir")
+    assert list_dir_tool is not None, "list_dir not registered"
+
+    region = os.getenv("AWS_REGION", "ap-southeast-2")
+    client = BedrockClient(model_id=_HAIKU_45_MODEL_ID, region=region, mock_mode=False)
+
+    tool_schema = [{
+        "name": "list_dir",
+        "description": list_dir_tool.description,
+        "input_schema": list_dir_tool.input_schema,
+    }]
+
+    # Round-trip 1: user asks, model returns tool_use.
+    messages = [{
+        "role": "user",
+        "content": "List the files in the current directory using the list_dir tool, then summarize.",
+    }]

+        tools=tool_schema,
+        max_tokens=512,
+    )

+    tool_call = response.tool_calls[0]

+
+    # Execute the tool locally.

+    assert isinstance(tool_result, str), f"list_dir returned non-string: {type(tool_result)}"
+
+    # Round-trip 2: send tool_result, get final text.
+    # Bedrock requires the assistant tool_use turn first, then a user
+    # turn with tool_result; we reconstruct the assistant content shape.
+    messages.append({

+        "content": [

+            {

+    })
+    messages.append({

+    assert response2.stop_reason == "end_turn", (

+    )

 218:         # + dynamic (uncached) blocks. Bedrock supports prompt caching natively
 219:         # via cache_control blocks in content. No anthropic_beta header needed.
 220:         # Haiku 4.5: min 4096 tokens/checkpoint. Sonnet 4.5: min 1024.
 221:         cache_active = CONFIG.enable_prompt_cache and self.prompt_cache_supported
 222:         if cache_active and isinstance(system, list):
 223:             # Already formatted as cache blocks by caller â€” pass as-is
 224:             system_field = system
 225:             use_cache = True
 226:         elif cache_active and isinstance(system, str):
 227:             # Split at the dynamic boundary marker if present, else cache full prompt
 228:             _CACHE_BOUNDARY = "\n\n# === DYNAMIC ==="
 229:             if _CACHE_BOUNDARY in system:
 230:                 static_part, dynamic_part = system.split(_CACHE_BOUNDARY, 1)
 231:                 # Bedrock rejects empty/whitespace text blocks â€” only add dynamic if non-empty
 232:                 if dynamic_part.strip():
 233:                     system_field = [
 234:                         {
 235:                             "type": "text",
 236:                             "text": static_part,
 237:                             "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
 238:                         },
 239:                         {"type": "text", "text": dynamic_part},
 240:                     ]
 241:                 else:
 242:                     system_field = [
 243:                         {
 244:                             "type": "text",
 245:                             "text": static_part,
 246:                             "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
 247:                         },
 248:                     ]
 249:             else:
 250:                 # No boundary â€” cache the whole prompt as static
 251:                 system_field = [
 252:                     {
 253:                         "type": "text",
 254:                         "text": system,
 255:                         "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
 256:                     },
 257:                 ]
 258:             use_cache = True
 259:         else:
 260:             system_field = system
 261:             use_cache = False
 262: 
 263:         body: Dict[str, Any] = {
 264:             "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31",
 265:             "max_tokens": max_tokens,
 266:             "system": system_field,
 267:             "messages": messages,
 268:         }
 269:         # Note: Bedrock prompt caching is activated by cache_control blocks in
 270:         # content. No anthropic_beta header needed (that header is for the direct
 271:         # Anthropic API only).
 272: 
 273:         # Extended thinking mode (requires temperature=1).
 274:         # PS Issue #4: this block runs on EVERY chat() call when thinking_enabled
 275:         # is True â€” not just first message. The model decides per turn whether
 276:         # to USE the budget. tests/unit/test_bedrock.py asserts this contract.
 277:         if thinking_enabled:
 278:             body["thinking"] = {
 279:                 "type": "enabled",
 280:                 "budget_tokens": min(max(thinking_budget, 1024), 16000),
 281:             }
 282:             body["temperature"] = 1  # Required for thinking mode
 283:         else:
 284:             body["temperature"] = temperature
 285: 
 286:         if tools:
 287:             body["tools"] = tools
 288: 
 289:         # V4.9.4: jittered exponential backoff on transient/throttle errors.
 290:         # Cache-validation: strip cache blocks and retry once (existing v4.1 #14).
 291:         attempt = 0
 292:         last_exc: Optional[Exception] = None
 293:         while True:
 294:             try:
 295:                 response = self.client.invoke_model(
 296:                     modelId=self.model_id,
 297:                     body=json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")),
 298:                     contentType="application/json",
 299:                 )
 300:                 break  # success
 301:             except Exception as e:
 302:                 last_exc = e
 303:                 category, recovery, debug_msg = ErrorClassifier.classify(e)
 304: 
 305:                 # Cache-validation: strip cache blocks, retry once
 306:                 if (
 307:                     category == BedrockErrorCategory.VALIDATION_CACHE
 308:                     and use_cache
 309:                     and self.prompt_cache_supported
 310:                 ):
 311:                     logging.warning(
 312:                         f"[BEDROCK] Prompt cache not supported by this model/region, falling back: {debug_msg}"
 313:                     )
 314:                     self.prompt_cache_supported = False
 315:                     if isinstance(system, str):
 316:                         body["system"] = system
 317:                     else:
 318:                         body["system"] = "\n\n".join(
 319:                             b.get("text", "") for b in system if isinstance(b, dict)
 320:                         )
 321:                     use_cache = False
 322:                     continue
 323: 
 324:                 # Throttle / transient / etc.: retry with jitter
 325:                 if RetryPolicy.should_retry(attempt, recovery):
 326:                     sleep_s = RetryPolicy.backoff_seconds(attempt)
 327:                     logging.warning(
 328:                         f"[BEDROCK] {category} (recovery={recovery}, attempt={attempt + 1}/"
 329:                         f"{RetryPolicy.MAX_RETRIES + 1}, sleep={sleep_s:.1f}s): {debug_msg}"
 330:                     )
 331:                     time.sleep(sleep_s)
 332:                     attempt += 1
 333:                     continue
 334: 
 335:                 # Anything else: surface it
 336:                 logging.error(f"[BEDROCK] {category} (recovery={recovery}, no-retry): {debug_msg}")
 337:                 raise
 338: 
 339:         result = json.loads(response["body"].read())
 340:         return self._parse(result)
 341: 
 342:     # ---------- response parsing ----------
 343: 
 344:     def _parse(self, result: dict) -> Response:
 345:         """Parse Bedrock response into Response value type (v4 verbatim)."""
 346:         text = ""
 347:         thinking = ""
 348:         tool_calls: List[ToolCall] = []
 349:         for block in result.get("content", []):
 350:             block_type = block.get("type")
 351:             if block_type == "text":
 352:                 text += block.get("text", "")
 353:             elif block_type == "thinking":
 354:                 thinking += block.get("thinking", "")
 355:             elif block_type == "tool_use":
 356:                 tool_calls.append(
 357:                     ToolCall(
 358:                         id=block.get("id", ""),
 359:                         name=block.get("name", ""),
 360:                         input=block.get("input", {}),
 361:                     )
 362:                 )
 363:         return Response(
 364:             text=text,
 365:             tool_calls=tool_calls,
 366:             stop_reason=result.get("stop_reason", ""),
 367:             usage=result.get("usage", {}),
 368:             thinking=thinking,
 369:         )

 377:         messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],

 380:         model_id: Optional[str] = None,
 381:     ) -> Optional[int]:

 384:         Returns the token count as int, or None on failure / mock mode.

 387:         Compactor (Block A) cannot make safe context-budget decisions.

 389:         Falls through to None when:
 390:           - mock_mode is True (no Bedrock contact)

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:569:- **v4** (`compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:5433`): `[sys.executable, temp_path]` — runs Python with the user's site-packages reachable.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:570:- **v5 Phase 5**: `[sys.executable, "-I", temp_path]` — adds the `-I` (isolated mode) flag. This prevents the user's pip cache, PYTHONPATH, and `~/.pythonrc` from leaking into the sandboxed code. The closure-based runtime sandbox still enforces the import allowlist; `-I` just hardens the boundary so `sys.path` doesn't include `~/.local/lib/...` packages the agent never declared.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:577:- (No rows for security/ files — pure v4 reuse, no Runnable adoption.)

compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:593:- **REPLACEMENT** of v4's monolithic 914-LOC `SYSTEM_PROMPT` f-string with file-per-section `prompt/*.md` files + `prompt/sections.py` registry + `core/cache.py` cache-block builder.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:607:- Code complexity: 19-20 small `.md` files (most ≤1KB each) + `prompt/sections.py` (~150 LOC) + `prompt/__init__.py` (~50 LOC) + `core/cache.py` (~200 LOC). Replacement of v4's 914-LOC f-string. Net: similar LOC, drastically better reviewability.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:628:| 7 | `answer_preference.md` | 100 | Chat vs files; never create summary.md without explicit ask. |
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:654:- Phase 6 formalises the boundary: `prompt/__init__.py:build_system_prompt(ctx)` returns a list of message-content blocks, with the cache-boundary marker between the static and dynamic groups.
compact_v5\_status\V5_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:662:- v5 sections are STATIC `.md` FILES, not TS function returns. Justified because: (a) auditing is grep-friendly, (b) no v5 section currently needs runtime computation, (c) per-section token caps are mechanically enforceable on text files. Constraint = `Bedrock` (Bedrock prompt cache rewards static byte-stable prefixes; runtime function returns add a hashing step).

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0-iter2.md:1953:- **v5 Phase 5**: `[sys.executable, "-I", temp_path]` â€” adds the `-I` (isolated mode) flag. This prevents the user's pip cache, PYTHONPATH, and `~/.pythonrc` from leaking into the sandboxed code. The closure-based runtime sandbox still enforces the import allowlist; `-I` just hardens the boundary so `sys.path` doesn't include `~/.local/lib/...` packages the agent never declared.

compact_v5\docs\PS_actual_use_problems.md:265:- **Repetitive read pattern across cell-rendered vs raw-JSON views**: when grepping a `.ipynb` file, line numbers from grep map to raw JSON, but `read_file` on `.ipynb` returns a cell-rendered view with different effective line numbers. The agent wasted ~5 read attempts on this mismatch. **Future fix**: either (a) make grep on .ipynb return cell-rendered line numbers too, or (b) always use `notebook_edit` style cell-by-cell access for .ipynb files.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:28:- **v4**: `BedrockClient` (`compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:2378`) imported `CONFIG` at module top, creating an implicit Phase-1/Phase-8 circular dependency once the module split happens.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:65:- **v4**: `PLAN_MODE_ALLOWED_TOOLS` set at `sagemaker_agent.py:6905` filtered tools by name at dispatch time (`:9390`). MCP tools landed in `TOOLS` dict alongside built-ins, so the dispatch-time filter caught them too — but the filter was ad-hoc and easily bypassed by callers reading the TOOLS dict directly.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:101:- **v5 prompt**: says "Regex search across files. ... Pattern syntax: Python `re` semantics — literal braces don't need escaping; backreferences and named groups are supported."
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:111:- **Runnable prompt for read_file**: "This tool can only read files, not directories. To read a directory, use an `ls` command via the Bash tool."
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:151:### 4.3 edit_file now rejects edits to externally-modified files (stale-check, was implicit in v4)
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:182:### 5.1 Security policies are now in their own files (auditability)
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:184:- **v5**: `security/dangerous_patterns.py` (CATASTROPHIC + DANGEROUS_PATTERNS + allowlists), `security/dangerous_python.py` (DANGEROUS_PYTHON + ALLOWED/BLOCKED + members), `security/high_risk.py` (HIGH_RISK_TOOLS), `security/manager.py` (the class + helpers). A reviewer scans 5 small files.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:195:- **v5**: `security.manager.rebuild_singleton_for_tests()` returns a fresh SecurityManager bound to current CONFIG state. `security.__init__.py` exposes `SECURITY` via module-level `__getattr__` so callers always get the current singleton — no stale references.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:206:- **v4**: bash and python_exec were marked high-risk in the approval-prompt UX (`HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {"bash", "python_exec", "task", "web_fetch"}` at sagemaker_agent.py:10487) but neither tool exposed an `is_destructive` flag — the approval prompt's "always allow" suppression worked for OTHER tools but always asked for these four.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:228:### 6.1 SYSTEM_PROMPT replaced by 19 file-per-section .md files
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:229:- **v4** (`compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py:8029-8178`): a single 914-LOC f-string with embedded `# === DYNAMIC ===` boundary marker.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:230:- **v5**: 19 reviewable .md files in `prompt/` + `prompt/sections.py` registry + `prompt/__init__.py:build_system_prompt(ctx)`. Each file has a hard token cap; CI gate fails on growth.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:307:- **v4**: `Agent.run` was inline in the 12K-LOC `sagemaker_agent.py` monolith starting at line 8650; ~1500 LOC mixing budget gate, microcompact, context_collapse, 2-stage compaction, skill auto-trigger, sub-agent dispatch, file-read state, retry, error classification, tool dispatch, output_fn callback contract.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:320:- **Acceptance test** (`test_tool_search_round_trip_promotes_deferred_tool`): turn 1 `tools=` excludes view_image; model calls `tool_search(select:view_image)`; turn 2 `tools=` includes view_image schema. End-to-end Phase 7 contract validated.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:328:- **v4**: `IterationBudget` was inline in the monolith at `sagemaker_agent.py:8190`. Adopted from Hermes (`run_agent.py:170`) in v4.9.4. Default 90 → bumped in-place to 600 in v4.10.10 because Hermes's 90 was too tight for SageMaker dev work.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:343:- **File-read state tracking**: deferred — Phase 4 introduced `_files_read` lock; Phase 8 doesn't reset it on compact because Phase 8 doesn't compact.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:352:- **v4**: `_run_task_tool` ~600 LOC inline at sagemaker_agent.py:8350. Mixes AGENT_TYPES lookup, env-details probing, handoff-block assembly, worktree isolation, parallel dispatch, model override, sub-client construction, child Agent instantiation, and tool dispatch — all in one method.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:373:- **v4**: validates against `AGENT_TYPES` dict and returns "Error: Unknown agent type 'X'. Available: ..." (sagemaker_agent.py:8366).
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:379:- **v4**: `_sanitize_handoff` replaces in-content `# === DYNAMIC ===` so a user-supplied AGENT_STATUS can't corrupt cache-block splitting (sagemaker_agent.py:7754).
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:395:- **v4**: SkillManager is ~470 LOC inline at sagemaker_agent.py:2684 — discover/list/read/active/auto-trigger/list_for_prompt/propose_patch/apply_proposal/etc all in one class buried in the monolith.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:437:- **v4**: `create_chat_ui` is ~2000 LOC inline at sagemaker_agent.py:9735. Mixes session state, HTML rendering, model-switcher, mock-mode toggle, AWS-scope toggle, full chat-display rendering, todo list, status bar — all in one function.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_FUNCTIONAL_CHANGES_FROM_V4.md:438:- **v5**: split into `agent/__init__.py` (Agent wrapper class) + `entry.py` (cell-0 imports) + `ui/chat_ui.py` (~150 LOC factory) + `ui/widgets.py` (PS Issue #2/#4 widgets) + `chat.ipynb` (4 cells) + `chat.md` (companion). Each piece independently testable.

compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:98:- **Adopted (ADAPT) with truthfulness correction**: v5 prompt says "Regex search across files." and "Pattern syntax: Python `re` semantics".
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:105:- **Why we added the v4 note**: v4's glob has this fallback (sagemaker_agent.py:4867), and SageMaker users frequently work inside a sub-directory of a parent git repo where the upper levels are in allowed_paths. Without the prompt note, the model wouldn't know that searching from the workspace root might silently extend to the parent.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:106:- **Better than Runnable**: v5 glob can find files in adjacent project dirs without the model needing to know about the allowed_paths feature.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:114:- **Source**: v4's `SecurityManager.validate_path` at `compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py`.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:125:- **Adopted (ADAPT)**: `tools/write_file.py:_DESCRIPTION` keeps Runnable's "MUST read first before overwriting" rule and the "prefer Edit for modifying existing files" steering.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:126:- **What we dropped**: Runnable's "NEVER create *.md / README files unless explicitly requested" + "no emojis" rules. These are policy rules that belong in the v5 main system prompt at Phase 6 (per ADR-002 file-per-section), not in the per-tool description. Per-tool descriptions should describe MECHANICS, not POLICY — duplicating policy across every tool would bloat the per-turn token cost.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:153:- **Source**: v4 `_FILES_READ` set + `_FILE_READ_TIMES` dict + `_FILES_READ_LOCK` threading.Lock at `compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py` (around line 4200).
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:158:- **Source**: v4's notebook_edit at `sagemaker_agent.py:5921` used `tempfile.mkstemp` + `os.replace` inline.
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:188:| **5** | **v4** | **Python 3.11 portability** | **Closure-sandbox allowlist now includes `_collections_abc`, `keyword`, `reprlib`, `_pyio`, `_compat_pickle`, `_warnings` — observed transitive imports needed for `import json` to work on Python 3.11. v4 hit this gap but never patched.** |
compact_v5\docs\PS_V5_LEARNINGS_FROM_REPOS.md:190:| **5** | **v4** | **dynamic SECURITY re-export** | **`security/__init__.py` uses module-level `__getattr__` for `SECURITY` — callers that did `from security import SECURITY` always get the CURRENT singleton, even after rebuild. Eliminates stale-reference bugs.** |

Constants split into `dangerous_patterns.py` + `dangerous_python.py`; class + helpers in `manager.py`; HIGH_RISK_TOOLS in `high_risk.py`; package re-exports in `__init__.py` (with dynamic `SECURITY` via module-level `__getattr__`).

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-0.md:1953:- **v5 Phase 5**: `[sys.executable, "-I", temp_path]` â€” adds the `-I` (isolated mode) flag. This prevents the user's pip cache, PYTHONPATH, and `~/.pythonrc` from leaking into the sandboxed code. The closure-based runtime sandbox still enforces the import allowlist; `-I` just hardens the boundary so `sys.path` doesn't include `~/.local/lib/...` packages the agent never declared.

compact_v5\docs\htmls\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT_v4.html:98:  <b>v4.10.7</b> — destructive-command hardening: ~50 new bash <code>DANGEROUS_PATTERNS</code> + ~12 python <code>DANGEROUS_PYTHON</code> patterns covering cloud destructive subcommands (AWS/GCP/Azure/PaaS/IaC/orchestration), git destructive flags, storage/volume tooling (<code>lvremove</code>, <code>mkfs</code>, <code>dd of=/dev/</code>, <code>zfs destroy</code>, <code>cryptsetup luksClose</code>), persistence (<code>crontab -r</code>, <code>systemctl disable/stop</code>), DB CLI inline (<code>DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE FROM/FLUSHALL/SHUTDOWN</code>), system-path overwrite, perm lockout, <code>curl|sh</code>, and Python destructive (<code>cursor.execute DROP</code>, SQLAlchemy <code>drop_all</code>, Mongo <code>dropDatabase</code>, <code>shutil.rmtree</code> on system paths). HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch} excluded from Always-Approve UI shortcut — no permanent bypass possible. Cross-surface: same denylist mirrored into <code>~/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-safety.sh</code> (Claude Code global) + <code>Learning_Factory/hooks/pre-bash-safety.sh</code> (LF source of truth, auto-installed by <code>setup.sh</code> on new machines). Arcsage_OPC inherits via the global hook. Codex CLI has no PreToolUse hook surface — relies on its own elevated sandbox.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\HERMES_VS_CODING_AGENT_v4.html:100:  <b>v4.10.9</b> — backtick eval+downloader parity (2026-04-29). Closes Codex's third local-hook finding from the v4.10.8 round in v4 itself: bare backtick command-substitution form of <code>eval</code> + remote-fetcher/decoder. <strong>Defense-in-depth only</strong> — <code>eval</code> is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, so all <code>eval</code> forms fail at allowlist before regex runs. Pattern is narrow-by-design (requires backtick AND a fetcher/decoder; legitimate <code>eval `date`</code>/<code>eval `git ...`</code> would NOT trip). Zero new false-positive risk.

compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5291:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3591:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:30:   "source": "# ============================================================\n# LAUNCH AGENT WITH CONFIGURATION\n# ============================================================\n\nfrom sagemaker_agent import CONFIG, create_chat_ui\nfrom IPython.display import display, HTML\n\n# Security & cost settings (previously in agent_config.json)\nCONFIG.aws_bedrock_only = True          # Block ALL AWS services except Bedrock\nCONFIG.require_tool_approval = True     # Show Approve/Deny dialog before execution\nCONFIG.session_cost_limit = 1.0         # Max $1.00 per session (warns at 80%, stops at 100%)\n\n# Custom slash commands: /review, /explain, /test\nCONFIG.custom_commands = {\n    \"review\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Read $ARGUMENTS and perform a thorough code review using this checklist:\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 1. Security (CRITICAL)\\n\"\n            \"Check: hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, command injection, XSS, path traversal, input validation, auth checks, sensitive data in logs\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 2. Code Quality (HIGH)\\n\"\n            \"Check: functions <50 lines, nesting <4 levels, specific error handling, clear naming, no dead code, no debug statements, DRY, consistent style\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 3. Performance (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: N+1 queries, O(n^2) algorithms, missing caching, unnecessary allocations, lazy processing for large collections\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 4. Architecture (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: separation of concerns, follows existing patterns, no circular deps, config externalized\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 5. Testing (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: critical paths covered, edge cases handled, tests independent, error paths tested\\n\"\n            \"\\n## Output: Summary, Issues (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with file:line), Positive observations, Suggestions, Rating X/10\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Full code review with 5-category checklist (security, quality, performance, architecture, testing)\",\n        \"agent\": \"plan\"\n    },\n    \"explain\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Read $ARGUMENTS and explain thoroughly:\\n\"\n            \"1. PURPOSE: What does this code do? What problem does it solve?\\n\"\n            \"2. ARCHITECTURE: How is it structured? What are the main components/classes/functions?\\n\"\n            \"3. DATA FLOW: How does data move through the code? Trace a typical request/call.\\n\"\n            \"4. KEY DECISIONS: What design patterns are used? Why were they chosen?\\n\"\n            \"5. DEPENDENCIES: What does it depend on? What depends on it?\\n\"\n            \"6. EDGE CASES: What error handling exists? What could go wrong?\\n\"\n            \"Use concrete examples from the actual code. Reference specific line numbers.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Deep code explanation (purpose, architecture, data flow, patterns, dependencies, edge cases)\"\n    },\n    \"test\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Read $ARGUMENTS and write comprehensive tests:\\n\"\n            \"1. Happy path: normal expected behavior\\n\"\n            \"2. Edge cases: empty input, None, boundaries, duplicates, max values\\n\"\n            \"3. Error cases: invalid input, missing data, permission errors, timeouts\\n\"\n            \"4. Integration: how components work together\\n\"\n            \"Use pytest style. Each test: Arrange, Act, Assert. Test names describe what is tested.\\n\"\n            \"Target: minimum 8 test functions with good coverage of all branches.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Generate comprehensive test suite (happy path, edge cases, error cases, integration)\"\n    },\n    \"verify\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Run 6-phase verification on the current workspace:\\n\"\n            \"Phase 1 BUILD: run build/compile if applicable (pip install -e . / npm run build)\\n\"\n            \"Phase 2 TYPES: run type checker (mypy/pyright/tsc) if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 3 LINT: run linter (ruff/flake8/eslint) if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 4 TESTS: run test suite (pytest/npm test) with coverage if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 5 SECURITY: grep for hardcoded secrets, .env files, debug statements\\n\"\n            \"Phase 6 DIFF: git diff to review all changes\\n\"\n            \"\\nOutput a VERIFICATION REPORT: each phase PASS/FAIL/SKIP, issues found, ready for PR: YES/NO\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"6-phase verification: build, types, lint, tests, security scan, diff review\"\n    },\n    \"standards\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Review $ARGUMENTS against these coding standards:\\n\"\n            \"NAMING: descriptive vars, verb-noun functions, PascalCase classes, UPPER_SNAKE constants\\n\"\n            \"FUNCTIONS: single responsibility, <50 lines, <4 params, <4 nesting, early returns\\n\"\n            \"ERRORS: specific exceptions (not bare except), no swallowed errors, user-friendly messages\\n\"\n            \"PRINCIPLES: KISS, DRY, YAGNI\\n\"\n            \"Fix any violations found. Show before/after for each fix.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Apply coding standards (naming, functions, errors, KISS/DRY/YAGNI)\"\n    },\n}\n\n# Apply configuration from widgets above\nCONFIG.model_id = AVAILABLE_MODELS[model_dropdown.value]\nCONFIG.region = REGION  # Sydney\nCONFIG.workspace = workspace_input.value\nCONFIG.max_turns = max_turns_slider.value\nCONFIG.mock_mode = mock_toggle.value\nCONFIG.temperature = TEMPERATURE_OPTIONS[temperature_dropdown.value]\nCONFIG.thinking_enabled = thinking_checkbox.value\nCONFIG.thinking_budget = THINKING_BUDGET_OPTIONS[thinking_budget_dropdown.value]\n\n# Display current config\nthinking_str = f\"Thinking: On (budget: {CONFIG.thinking_budget})\" if CONFIG.thinking_enabled else \"Thinking: Off\"\ndisplay(HTML(f\"\"\"\n<div style=\"background:#1e3a1e;padding:10px;border-radius:5px;margin:10px 0;color:#d4d4d4;\">\n<b>Configuration Applied</b><br>\nModel: {model_dropdown.value} | Region: Sydney | Temp: {CONFIG.temperature}<br>\n{thinking_str} | Mock: {'Yes' if CONFIG.mock_mode else 'No'}\n</div>\n\"\"\"))\n\n# Launch the chat interface\ncreate_chat_ui()"
compact_v5\_status\codex_reviews\block-b-iter1.md:5292:compact_v5/_phase_2\codex_review\CODEX_REVIEW_v2.md:3592:.\_archive\compact_v3\ship\chat.ipynb:35:   "source": "---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| Action | How |\n|--------|-----|\n| **Send message** | Type in input box, press Send |\n| **Stop agent** | Click Stop button |\n| **Check cost** | Type `/cost` |\n| **Code review** | Type `/review filename.py` |\n| **Explain code** | Type `/explain filename.py` |\n| **Generate tests** | Type `/test filename.py` |\n| **Verify project** | Type `/verify` |\n| **Apply standards** | Type `/standards filename.py` |\n| **Revert file** | Type `/revert filename.py` or `/revert all` |\n| **Compact context** | Click Compact button (or auto at 80%) |\n| **Clean traces** | Click Clean button (removes audit/snapshots, keeps sessions) |\n| **Save/Load** | Save button (auto-saves each message) / Session dropdown + Load |\n\n## Quick Start Examples\n\n| Task | What to type |\n|------|-------------|\n| Read a file | \"Read app.py\" |\n| Find files | \"Find all Python files in this project\" |\n| Fix a bug | \"Read app.py, find the bug, and fix it\" |\n| Create chart | \"Create a bar chart from sales.csv showing revenue by product\" |\n| Create report | \"Create a Word report summarizing the data in results.csv\" |\n| Run command | \"Run git status\" |\n| Analyze image | \"Look at screenshot.png and describe what you see\" |\n| Search code | \"Find where authentication is handled in this codebase\" |\n\n## 22 Tools\n\n| Category | Tools | Approval? |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

|\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **File** | read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep, list_dir | write/edit need approval |\n| **Exec** | bash, python_exec | Both need approval |\n| **Docs** | create_word, create_excel, create_chart, create_pdf, create_markdown, create_notebook | Need approval |\n| **Intelligence** | view_image (vision), semantic_search (code search), web_fetch (URL fetch only) | web_fetch needs approval |\n| **Agents** | skill (load checklist), task (spawn sub-agent), ask_user (ask you a question) | task needs approval |\n| **State** | todo_write, todo_read | Auto |\n\n## Sub-Agents (via `/task` or the agent decides automatically)\n\n| Type | What it does | Tools | Max turns |\n|------|-------------|-------|-----------|\n| **build** | Build, compile, fix errors, run tests | All 22 | 25 |\n| **plan** | Architecture analysis, planning (read-only) | 11 (read + web + ask) | 15 |\n| **explore** | Fast file search, codebase navigation | 5 (read + grep + glob) | 10 |\n| **general** | General coding tasks | 11 (no doc tools) | 15 |\n| **review** | Security, quality, performance review | 6 (read + search + vision) | 10 |\n\n## Security (16 layers)\n\nThe agent runs inside a security sandbox. Key protections:\n- **Bash**: 70 allowed commands only. 75 dangerous patterns blocked. Files restricted to workspace.\n- **Python**: 63 regex patterns + AST import validation (67 allowed modules) + runtime sandbox on open/remove.\n- **AWS**: `aws_bedrock_only` blocks ALL AWS services except Bedrock (regex + AST + getattr enforcement).\n- **Approval dialog**: You see exact command/code and Approve or Deny before execution.\n- **Cost limit**: Stops agent if session cost exceeds your configured limit.\n- **Audit trail**: Every tool call logged with timestamp and integrity hash.\n\n## Model Pricing (Bedrock, Sydney region)\n\n| Model | Input / 1M tokens | Output / 1M tokens |\n|-------|-------------------|-------------------|\n| Claude 3 Haiku | $0.25 | $1.25 |\n| Claude 3.5 Haiku | $0.80 | $4.00 |\n| **Claude 4.5 Haiku (AU)** | **$1.10** | **$5.50** |\n| Claude 4.5 Sonnet (AU) | $3.30 | $16.50 |\n| Claude 4.5 Opus | $5.00 | $25.00 |\n| Claude 4.6 Opus (AU) | $5.50 | $27.50 |\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. You type a message \u2192 sent to Claude via Bedrock API\n2. Claude decides which tool to use \u2192 calls it (with your approval if needed)\n3. Tool runs, result sent back to Claude \u2192 Claude decides next step or gives final answer\n4. Repeats up to 60 turns per message (configurable)\n5. Context auto-compacts at 80% usage (prune old tool outputs, then LLM summarize if needed)\n\n## Token Overhead Per API Call\n\n| Component | Tokens |\n|-----------|--------|\n| System prompt | ~1,200 |\n| Tool schemas | ~1,800 (lazy-load: ~1,200 for coding tasks) |\n| Bedrock overhead | ~346 |\n| **Total per call** | **~3,350** |\n\n## Session Management\n\n| Feature | How |\n|---------|-----|\n| **Auto-save** | Every message auto-saves (messages, todos, metadata) |\n| **Load session** | Session dropdown + Load button |\n| **New session** | New button (clears all state) |\n| **Checkpoints** | `/checkpoint name` (saves snapshot, max 50) |\n\n## Commands vs Skills\n\n| Method | How | Depth | Persists? |\n|--------|-----|-------|-----------|\n| `/review app.py` | Inline command \u2014 sends condensed checklist once | ~15 lines | No (one-shot) |\n| `/skill use review` then \"review app.py\" | Loads full skill file into system prompt | ~83 lines | Yes (all messages until `/skill clear`) |\n| \"Read clara_prompts.py then review app.py\" | Your own custom prompt file | Unlimited | No (one-shot) |\n\n**Commands** = quick one-shot shortcuts (good enough for most tasks).\n**Skills** = persistent behavior change (full checklists, stays active across messages).\n**Custom prompts** = your own files (deepest, most flexible).\n\n### Using Skills (if skills/ folder is present)\n\n```\n/skill use review            \u2190 load review checklist (active until cleared)\nreview app.py                \u2190 agent follows full 83-line checklist\nreview utils.py              \u2190 still following same checklist\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n\n/skill use verify            \u2190 load 6-phase verification\nverify this project          \u2190 runs build, types, lint, tests, security, diff\n\n/skill use coding-standards  \u2190 load KISS/DRY/YAGNI rules\nfix app.py                   \u2190 agent applies standards while fixing\n/skill clear                 \u2190 deactivate\n```\n\n### Available Skills\n\n| Skill | Lines | What it does |\n|-------|-------|-------------|\n| `review` | 83 | 5-category code review (security/quality/performance/architecture/testing) with severity ratings |\n| `verify` | 147 | 6-phase verification with actual shell commands per language + structured report |\n| `coding-standards` | 153 | KISS, DRY, YAGNI, naming conventions, function design, error handling |\n| `report` | 45 | Report generation workflow (chart-first, then Word/PDF) |\n\nSkills are optional \u2014 the agent works without them. Commands cover the same categories with less detail.\n\n## Config\n\nDefault config is set in Cell 3 (before launch). Change model, temperature, thinking mode anytime in the chatbot UI during use.\n\nKey security settings (Cell 3):\n- `aws_bedrock_only = True` \u2014 blocks all AWS except Bedrock\n- `session_cost_limit = 1.0` \u2014 max $1 per session\n- `require_tool_approval = True` \u2014 approve/deny before execution"

Security (CRITICAL)\\n\"\n            \"Check: hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, command injection, XSS, path traversal, input validation, auth checks, sensitive data in logs\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 2. Code Quality (HIGH)\\n\"\n            \"Check: functions <50 lines, nesting <4 levels, specific error handling, clear naming, no dead code, no debug statements, DRY, consistent style\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 3. Performance (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: N+1 queries, O(n^2) algorithms, missing caching, unnecessary allocations, lazy processing for large collections\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 4. Architecture (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: separation of concerns, follows existing patterns, no circular deps, config externalized\\n\"\n            \"\\n## 5. Testing (MEDIUM)\\n\"\n            \"Check: critical paths covered, edge cases handled, tests independent, error paths tested\\n\"\n            \"\\n## Output: Summary, Issues (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with file:line), Positive observations, Suggestions, Rating X/10\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Full code review with 5-category checklist (security, quality, performance, architecture, testing)\",\n        \"agent\": \"plan\"\n    },\n    \"explain\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Read $ARGUMENTS and explain thoroughly:\\n\"\n            \"1. PURPOSE: What does this code do? What problem does it solve?\\n\"\n            \"2. ARCHITECTURE: How is it structured? What are the main components/classes/functions?\\n\"\n            \"3. DATA FLOW: How does data move through the code? Trace a typical request/call.\\n\"\n            \"4. KEY DECISIONS: What design patterns are used? Why were they chosen?\\n\"\n            \"5. DEPENDENCIES: What does it depend on? What depends on it?\\n\"\n            \"6. EDGE CASES: What error handling exists? What could go wrong?\\n\"\n            \"Use concrete examples from the actual code. Reference specific line numbers.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Deep code explanation (purpose, architecture, data flow, patterns, dependencies, edge cases)\"\n    },\n    \"test\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Read $ARGUMENTS and write comprehensive tests:\\n\"\n            \"1. Happy path: normal expected behavior\\n\"\n            \"2. Edge cases: empty input, None, boundaries, duplicates, max values\\n\"\n            \"3. Error cases: invalid input, missing data, permission errors, timeouts\\n\"\n            \"4. Integration: how components work together\\n\"\n            \"Use pytest style. Each test: Arrange, Act, Assert. Test names describe what is tested.\\n\"\n            \"Target: minimum 8 test functions with good coverage of all branches.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Generate comprehensive test suite (happy path, edge cases, error cases, integration)\"\n    },\n    \"verify\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Run 6-phase verification on the current workspace:\\n\"\n            \"Phase 1 BUILD: run build/compile if applicable (pip install -e . / npm run build)\\n\"\n            \"Phase 2 TYPES: run type checker (mypy/pyright/tsc) if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 3 LINT: run linter (ruff/flake8/eslint) if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 4 TESTS: run test suite (pytest/npm test) with coverage if available\\n\"\n            \"Phase 5 SECURITY: grep for hardcoded secrets, .env files, debug statements\\n\"\n            \"Phase 6 DIFF: git diff to review all changes\\n\"\n            \"\\nOutput a VERIFICATION REPORT: each phase PASS/FAIL/SKIP, issues found, ready for PR: YES/NO\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"6-phase verification: build, types, lint, tests, security scan, diff review\"\n    },\n    \"standards\": {\n        \"template\": (\n            \"Review $ARGUMENTS against these coding standards:\\n\"\n            \"NAMING: descriptive vars, verb-noun functions, PascalCase classes, UPPER_SNAKE constants\\n\"\n            \"FUNCTIONS: single responsibility, <50 lines, <4 params, <4 nesting, early returns\\n\"\n            \"ERRORS: specific exceptions (not bare except), no swallowed errors, user-friendly messages\\n\"\n            \"PRINCIPLES: KISS, DRY, YAGNI\\n\"\n            \"Fix any violations found. Show before/after for each fix.\"\n        ),\n        \"description\": \"Apply coding standards (naming, functions, errors, KISS/DRY/YAGNI)\"\n    },\n}\n\n# Apply configuration from widgets above\nCONFIG.model_id = AVAILABLE_MODELS[model_dropdown.value]\nCONFIG.region = REGION  # Sydney\nCONFIG.workspace = workspace_input.value\nCONFIG.max_turns = max_turns_slider.value\nCONFIG.mock_mode = mock_toggle.value\nCONFIG.temperature = TEMPERATURE_OPTIONS[temperature_dropdown.value]\nCONFIG.thinking_enabled = thinking_checkbox.value\nCONFIG.thinking_budget = THINKING_BUDGET_OPTIONS[thinking_budget_dropdown.value]\n\n# Display current config\nthinking_str = f\"Thinking: On (budget: {CONFIG.thinking_budget})\" if CONFIG.thinking_enabled else \"Thinking: Off\"\ndisplay(HTML(f\"\"\"\n<div style=\"background:#1e3a1e;padding:10px;border-radius:5px;margin:10px 0;color:#d4d4d4;\">\n<b>Configuration Applied</b><br>\nModel: {model_dropdown.value} | Region: Sydney | Temp: {CONFIG.temperature}<br>\n{thinking_str} | Mock: {'Yes' if CONFIG.mock_mode else 'No'}\n</div>\n\"\"\"))\n\n# Launch the chat interface\ncreate_chat_ui()"

compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:215:    <p class="subtitle">A secure AI coding assistant that runs inside AWS SageMaker notebooks. It reads your code, writes files, edits Jupyter notebooks surgically, creates documents, generates charts, and helps you build software &mdash; all through a chat interface. v4.10.0 shipped 5 Runnable-parity upgrades. v4.10.1 added Context Collapse + Sonnet 4.5 default. v4.10.2 softened the verify-contract. v4.10.3 added ship-gate verifier + cache-boundary regression test + many-skill stress test + clearer permission denials. v4.10.4 closed the largest remaining gap: sub-agents now receive a bounded work-context handoff block (AGENT_STATUS slice + active todos + recent changed files) on top of v4.10.0's env-details. v4.10.5 adopted 3 Learning_Factory prompt-only patterns: post-compact resume protocol, structured summary sections, skill self-patching 4-rule check. v4.10.6 added the html skill: presentation / design / flowchart / architecture HTML deliverables, with screenshot-iteration loop. v4.10.7 hardened destructive-command coverage: ~50 new bash patterns + ~12 python patterns spanning cloud / IaC / orchestration / storage / DB CLI / persistence / system-overwrite, HIGH_RISK_TOOLS excluded from Always-Approve UI, cross-surface mirrored into Claude Code + Learning_Factory hooks. v4.10.8 closed the residual obfuscation escape route (base64/xxd/eval pipe-to-shell now blocked across more interpreters) and hard-blocked recursive folder removal from the agent (`rm -r/-rf/-fr/-R/--recursive`, `rmdir`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `shutil.rmtree`, `os.rmdir`, `os.removedirs`, `Path(...).rmdir()`) — single-file cleanup still allowed; the 🧹 Clean button still works in-process. v4.10.9 closed Codex's third local-hook finding by adding a narrow backtick eval+downloader pattern (defense-in-depth only — eval was already excluded from the bash allowlist; zero new false-positive risk). v4.10.10 surfaced the previously-hardcoded `aws_bedrock_only` setting as a UI checkbox in cell 2 of `chat.ipynb` (default ticked = strict). Codex review on v4.10.10: PASS. 134/134 destructive-coverage tests + 122 v4 unit tests + 16/16 hook obfuscation self-test all green.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:268:                <div class="card-desc">~50 new bash <code>DANGEROUS_PATTERNS</code> covering cloud destructive subcommands (AWS/GCP/Azure/PaaS/IaC/orchestration), git destructive (remote-branch del, <code>branch -D</code>, <code>tag -d</code>, <code>reflog expire</code>, <code>restore .</code>), storage tools (<code>lvremove</code>, <code>mkfs</code>, <code>dd of=/dev/</code>, <code>zfs destroy</code>, <code>cryptsetup luksClose</code>), persistence (<code>crontab -r</code>, <code>systemctl disable/stop</code>, <code>pm2 delete</code>), DB CLI inline (<code>DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE FROM/FLUSHALL/SHUTDOWN</code>), system-path overwrite, perm lockout, <code>curl|sh</code>. ~12 new <code>DANGEROUS_PYTHON</code> patterns (<code>cursor.execute DROP</code>, SQLAlchemy <code>drop_all</code>, Mongo <code>dropDatabase/deleteMany</code>, Redis <code>flushall</code>, <code>os.unlink</code>/<code>shutil.rmtree</code> on system paths). <strong>HIGH_RISK_TOOLS = {bash, python_exec, task, web_fetch}</strong> excluded from Always-Approve UI shortcut — even with auto-approve on, these still prompt; the "Always Approve" button is hidden for them, so there's no UI path to a permanent bypass. Cross-surface: same denylist mirrored into <code>~/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-safety.sh</code> + Learning_Factory source-of-truth.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:278:                <div class="card-desc">Closes Codex's third local-hook finding from the v4.10.8 round in v4 itself: bare backtick command-substitution (<code>eval `curl ...`</code>, <code>eval `wget ...`</code>, <code>eval `base64 -d ...`</code>) was caught in the local hook but not v4. <strong>Defense-in-depth only</strong> — <code>eval</code> is already excluded from v4's bash allowlist, so all <code>eval</code> forms fail at allowlist before regex runs. The new pattern provides clear attack-specific messaging for the obfuscation case and parity with the local hook. <strong>Narrow-by-design</strong>: requires backtick AND a remote-fetcher (<code>curl</code>/<code>wget</code>/<code>fetch</code>) OR decoder (<code>base64</code>/<code>xxd</code>/<code>hexdump</code>). Legitimate uses like <code>eval `date`</code>, <code>eval `git ...`</code>, <code>eval `pwd`</code> would NOT trip even if <code>eval</code> were allowlisted. <strong>Zero new false-positive risk.</strong> 134-case test coverage (up from v4.10.8's 129) + 122 v4 unit tests still green.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:323:            <div><strong>Why does this matter?</strong> Without a coding agent, you write code yourself. With one, you describe what you want and the agent writes it. V3 can read files, edit code, run commands, create Word/Excel/PDF documents, generate charts, analyze images, search your codebase, and manage tasks &mdash; all through conversation.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:371:                <div class="flow-box flow-tool" onclick="document.getElementById('fd-files').showModal()">
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:453:        <strong style="color:var(--amber)">HOW:</strong> The <code>Agent.run()</code> method (515 lines) orchestrates this. It includes:<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:468:        <strong style="color:var(--green)">WHAT:</strong> The Context Manager tracks how much of the window is used and automatically compresses old conversation when it gets too full. It also caches files to avoid re-reading them.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:473:        &bull; <strong>File Cache</strong> &mdash; LRU cache (100 entries) with mtime validation. Skips re-reading files already in context.<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:479:<dialog id="fd-files" class="modal" onclick="if(event.target===this)this.close()">
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:483:        <strong style="color:var(--blue)">WHY:</strong> A coding agent needs to read and modify files — that's its primary job. These 6 tools let it navigate your codebase like a human developer would.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:485:        &bull; <strong>read_file</strong> &mdash; reads file contents (supports offset/limit for large files, max 500 lines default)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:486:        &bull; <strong>write_file</strong> &mdash; creates new files (must read first if file exists — safety check)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:487:        &bull; <strong>edit_file</strong> &mdash; find-and-replace in files (shows diff of what changed)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:488:        &bull; <strong>glob</strong> &mdash; find files by pattern (e.g., **/*.py finds all Python files)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:489:        &bull; <strong>grep</strong> &mdash; search inside files by regex (like Ctrl+F across entire codebase, max 50 results)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:499:        <strong style="color:var(--blue)">WHY:</strong> Reading and writing files isn't enough — the agent needs to run code, install packages, run tests, and execute commands. These are the most powerful (and most guarded) tools.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:503:        <strong style="color:var(--amber)">HOW:</strong> Both tools require your approval before executing. You see the exact command/code in an Approve/Deny dialog. Execution has a timeout (600s for bash, 300s for Python) and a global budget (40 calls, 900 seconds per session). Auto-lint checks Python files after writing for syntax errors.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:518:        &bull; <strong>create_markdown</strong> &mdash; .md files with full formatting<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:531:        &bull; <strong>semantic_search</strong> &mdash; searches codebase by meaning using Titan embeddings. Python files chunked by function/class (AST-aware).<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:533:        &bull; <strong>skill</strong> &mdash; loads instruction files that teach the agent new behaviors (4 skills: review, verify, coding-standards, report)<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:537:        <strong style="color:var(--amber)">HOW:</strong> Sub-agents run in separate threads with their own context and tool access. Skills are Markdown files in the <code>skills/</code> folder. Semantic search uses AWS Titan Embed v2 for vector embeddings.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:545:        <strong style="color:var(--blue)">WHY:</strong> The AI can make mistakes or be tricked by malicious prompts. Without security, it could delete files, read secrets, call AWS services, or exfiltrate data. The Security Gate prevents all of this.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:592:        <strong style="color:var(--amber)">HOW:</strong> Session saves use atomic writes (temp file + os.replace) with thread locking to prevent corruption. If the agent used tools, their results are truncated to max 1,500 lines / 30KB to fit in context. A cleanup button (&#129529; Clean) removes audit logs, snapshots, and index files while keeping sessions.

Like Ctrl+F but across your entire codebase.</div><div class="card-tags"><span class="tag tag-blue">File</span><span class="tag tag-green">Safe</span></div></div>

Shows sizes and types.</div><div class="card-tags"><span class="tag tag-blue">File</span><span class="tag tag-green">Safe</span></div></div>
