compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:753:                    <strong>Layer 3 &mdash; Path boundary:</strong> Can only access files inside your workspace. /etc/passwd? Blocked.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:782:            V3's security follows the principle of least privilege: the agent has access to tools within your workspace only. System files, AWS resources beyond Bedrock, network access, and credentials are all blocked by separate enforcement layers. Each tool call is validated before execution, and destructive operations require explicit user approval.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:800:                <tr><td><strong>Language</strong></td><td>Python (single file)</td><td>TypeScript (monorepo, 195 files)</td><td>TypeScript</td><td>Rust + TypeScript</td></tr>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:812:                <tr><td><strong>Session Persistence</strong></td><td class="check">JSON files</td><td class="check">SQLite</td><td>Memory file</td><td class="cross">No</td></tr>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:822:            <div><strong>V3 learned from OpenCode.</strong> The architecture patterns &mdash; ReAct loop, context compaction, skill system, sub-agents, MCP support, config files &mdash; all originated in OpenCode's TypeScript codebase. V3 reimplemented them in Python for SageMaker, added document creation (6 tools), image understanding, cost tracking with budgets, and 16 security layers that OpenCode doesn't have.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:849:                    V3 doesn't always send all 24 tools. Document creation tools (Word, Excel, Chart, PDF, Markdown, Notebook) are <strong>excluded</strong> unless your recent messages mention doc-related keywords.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:898:                <div class="card-desc">Read-only + web_fetch + ask_user. For architecture analysis, planning, and research. Cannot modify files.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:904:                <div class="card-desc">Fast file search only. For quickly finding files, reading code, grepping patterns. Minimal and fast.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:942:                    <strong style="color:var(--amber)">HOW:</strong> The Compactor class (200 lines) handles this. File Cache (LRU, 100 entries) prevents re-reading files. Smart Truncation caps tool output at 1,500 lines / 30KB with head+tail split.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1001:                <tr><td><strong>disable_local_traces</strong></td><td>false</td><td>Stealth mode: no audit/session/snapshot files written</td></tr>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1100:        <strong>read_file</strong> reads a file and returns its contents. You can specify offset (start line) and limit (how many lines) to read just the part you need &mdash; important for large files.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1111:        <strong>bash</strong> runs shell commands like you would in a terminal. "ls -la" to list files, "pip install pandas" to install packages, "git status" to check git. Every command passes through 3 security layers before running.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1127:        <strong>Markdown (.md)</strong> &mdash; Formatted text files.
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1129:    <div class="explain">No other coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Cline) can natively create Word docs or Excel spreadsheets. They can only create text files. V3 was built for data scientists and analysts who need to generate reports, not just code.</div>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1137:        <strong>semantic_search</strong> &mdash; Searches your codebase by <em>meaning</em>, not just keywords. If you search "authentication logic", it finds code related to login/auth even if those exact words aren't used. Uses AWS Titan embeddings to convert code into vectors, then finds the most similar chunks. Python files are split by function/class (AST-aware), so results are more meaningful than line-based search.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\v4_architecture.html:1147:        <strong>skill</strong> &mdash; Loads a skill file (Markdown with instructions) into the agent's system prompt. Skills teach the agent new behaviors: "review" makes it do code reviews, "verify" makes it run 6-phase verification, "coding-standards" enforces style rules. Skills are stored in the <code>skills/</code> folder as SKILL.md files.<br><br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:185:<p>The Complete Runnable Architecture E-Book &mdash; 2,010 TypeScript files, 69 modules, every subsystem mapped.<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:198:  97 tests across 11 files green; per-phase Codex review (gpt-5.3-codex) caught 15 real correctness issues across the 7 releases — all fixed and re-verified before merging. Full plan: <code>compact_v4/docs/V4_10_0_PLAN.md</code>.</span>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:272:<p><b>Startup optimization pattern:</b> Fire expensive I/O (MDM, keychain) in parallel with module loading. Use feature flags for compile-time dead-code elimination. Lazy-load heavy modules (OpenTelemetry ~400KB). This gives Claude Code fast startup despite 2,010 files.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:390:<p>Workers can't see the coordinator's conversation. If you write "fix what worker A found", worker D has NO idea what worker A found. The coordinator must extract the key insight and include it in the prompt. This is the #1 mistake in multi-agent system design.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:396:<b>Prompt rule:</b> "Brief the agent like a colleague who just walked in &mdash; include context, what's been tried, and what to do."<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:465:<p>A background agent that reviews recent sessions and consolidates learnings into persistent memory files. Runs automatically when: &gt;24h since last consolidation AND &ge;5 sessions accumulated. Disk lock prevents concurrent consolidation.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:663:<p>60+ functions the AI can call: read files, run commands, search code, spawn agents, manage tasks. Each tool has a Zod-validated input schema, permission model, and execution pipeline.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:777:<p>File-based persistent memory: MEMORY.md index + individual topic.md files with YAML frontmatter. Survives across sessions. Sonnet classifier selects top 5 relevant memories per query.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:791:<p><b>Don't save:</b> code patterns (read the code), git history (use git log), debugging solutions (fix is in the code), architecture (read the files). Only save what's NOT derivable from the current project state. This prevents stale memories from overriding reality.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:827:<p><b>A plugin is a collection of:</b> skills, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, commands, agents, output styles. Each has a manifest.json, scoped installation (user/project/enterprise), and 24 specific error types for diagnostics. The key insight: plugins extend EVERY part of the system, not just tools.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:912:<p><b>What:</b> Keep agents independent.<br><b>Why:</b> Shared mutable state causes race conditions.<br><b>How:</b> AsyncLocalStorage for teammates. Git worktrees for files. Branded types prevent ID mixing. Getter/setter for bootstrap state.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:916:<p><b>What:</b> Understand results before passing them on.<br><b>Why:</b> Workers can't see parent context.<br><b>How:</b> Coordinator reads all findings, extracts key insights, includes specific details in worker prompts. Never "based on your findings, fix it."</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_DEEP_DIVE_RUNNABLE.html:931:<tr><td>Source files</td><td>2,010</td><td>Real agents need real engineering</td></tr>

compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:822:          <li><b>Fix 3 — Informative errors</b>: <code>validate_path</code>, <code>tool_read_file</code>, and <code>tool_glob</code> all now include workspace root + allowed roots + a <code>glob "**/filename"</code> or <code>bash find</code> recovery template. The agent self-corrects without user help.</li>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:843:          <li><b>What it is</b>: A 6-phase workflow for large multi-file tasks (5-30 files). The top-level agent becomes a COORDINATOR — it plans, decomposes, synthesizes, and directs. Sub-agents become WORKERS — they implement. <b>Roles are strictly separated</b>: coordinator never writes code, workers never plan.</li>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:844:          <li><b>When to use</b>: "Rename this function across the codebase", "Migrate all endpoints to new auth middleware", "Add logging to every handler". Any task touching 5+ files with independent units of work. If fewer than 5 files, just do it directly — don't batch. If changes are interdependent (file B depends on file A's output), do sequentially — don't batch.</li>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:845:          <li><b>Phase 1 — Research &amp; Plan</b>: Coordinator is read-only. Uses explore agents for parallel investigation. Finds ALL files, identifies build/test commands, defines the e2e verification recipe. Missing a file here = missing a worker later.</li>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:848:          <li><b>Phase 4 — Spawn Workers in Parallel</b>: Single message with N parallel <code>task</code> tool calls (subagent_type = build). <b>Each worker prompt is self-contained</b>: includes original user goal, this unit's task, exact files, change description, codebase conventions, e2e test recipe, and "commit when done". Workers have NO context from the coordinator's conversation.</li>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:852:        <p style="color:var(--muted);font-size:13px;margin-top:8px;"><b>Why this matters:</b> Without role separation, a single agent trying to refactor 20 files gets confused mid-stream, forgets earlier decisions, and loses the plot. Batch forces the "think once, execute many" discipline that humans use for migrations. The top agent holds the mental model; workers focus on one unit each. This is the exact pattern Runnable uses for its coordinator mode, ported to V4 as a skill. <b>Critical rule</b>: if you find yourself writing code in the coordinator, stop — that's the coordinator leaking into worker territory. Hand it to a <code>task</code> call instead.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_FLOWCHART_V4.html:1006:      <li><code>python -m py_compile compact_v4/MAIN/agent/sagemaker_agent.py compact_v4/MAIN/tests/test_v42_gap_closure.py</code></li>

Comparison source: runnable TypeScript snapshot under <code>compare_code/gg-claude-code-runnable</code>. V4.6 upgrade doc: <code>compact_v4/docs/V4_6_RUNNABLE_UPGRADE.md</code>.</p>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:356:// - AttachmentMessage: files, images, or data attached to the conversation
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:494:<tr><td><b>Isolation</b></td><td><b>Full isolation.</b> Each worker: own conversation history (clean context), own tool restrictions via <code>disallowedTools</code>, optional git worktree (isolated filesystem). Workers CANNOT see parent's conversation history.</td><td><b>Partial isolation.</b> Subgraphs have own internal state, but share input/output through parent state. No filesystem isolation. Same Python process.</td></tr>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:794: <td>Agents often re-read files they've already seen. Without this, each re-read wastes context space with identical content. The stub keeps context lean.</td>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:826:<b>What is enforcement?</b> Enforcement = stopping the AI from doing something dangerous. This is NOT the same as asking the AI nicely ("please don't delete files"). Enforcement means the system STRUCTURALLY PREVENTS the action. The AI can want to <code>rm -rf /</code> all it wants — the enforcement layer makes it impossible. This is the most important lesson from Claude Code.

compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:1270:<b>1. What's your deadline?</b> If you need something working in days, use LangGraph — it has batteries included. If you have weeks/months, Claude Code patterns give you more control.<br>
compact_v5\docs\htmls\PS_RUNNABLE_VS_LANGGRAPH.html:1299:<tr><td><b>Multi-agent</b></td><td>Workers need TRUE isolation (own context, own filesystem, own git worktree).</td><td>Shared state between agents is desirable. Subgraphs with supervisors.</td></tr>

  74: def _check(name: str, condition: bool, detail: str = "") -> bool:
  75:     status = "PASS" if condition else "FAIL"
  76:     suffix = f" -- {detail}" if detail else ""
  77:     print(f"  [{status}] {name}{suffix}")
  78:     return condition
  79: 
  80: 
  81: def main(zip_path: str = "../compact_v5.zip") -> int:
  82:     if not os.path.exists(zip_path):
  83:         print(f"ERROR: zip not found: {zip_path}")
  84:         return 1
  85: 
  86:     print(f"Verifying ship zip: {zip_path}")
  87:     print(f"Size: {os.path.getsize(zip_path):,} bytes\n")
  88: 
  89:     with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
  90:         names = z.namelist()
  91: 
  92:     print(f"Total entries: {len(names)}\n")
  93:     failures = 0
  94: 
  95:     print("== Required runtime files at root ==")
  96:     for required in sorted(REQUIRED_AT_ROOT):
  97:         if not _check(f"root/{required}", required in names):
  98:             failures += 1
  99: 
 100:     print("\n== Required package directories ==")
 101:     for pkg in sorted(REQUIRED_PACKAGES):
 102:         ok = any(n.startswith(pkg + "/__init__.py") or n == pkg + "/__init__.py" for n in names)
 103:         if not _check(f"{pkg}/__init__.py", ok):
 104:             failures += 1
 105: 
 106:     print("\n== Required tool modules ==")
 107:     for tool in sorted(REQUIRED_TOOLS):
 108:         ok = f"tools/{tool}" in names
 109:         if not _check(f"tools/{tool}", ok):
 110:             failures += 1
 111: 
 112:     print("\n== Required skill directories ==")
 113:     for skill in sorted(REQUIRED_SKILLS):
 114:         ok = any(n.startswith(f"skills/{skill}/SKILL.md") for n in names)
 115:         if not _check(f"skills/{skill}/SKILL.md", ok):
 116:             failures += 1
 117: 
 118:     print("\n== Forbidden patterns (dev artefacts) ==")
 119:     for pat in FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS:
 120:         offenders = [n for n in names if pat.search(n)]
 121:         if offenders:
 122:             failures += 1
 123:             sample = offenders[:3]
 124:             print(f"  [FAIL] pattern {pat.pattern!r} matches {len(offenders)} entries; sample: {sample}")
 125:         else:
 126:             print(f"  [PASS] pattern {pat.pattern!r} clean")
 127: 
 128:     print("\n== Result ==")
 129:     if failures:
 130:         print(f"  RESULT: FAIL -- {failures} assertion(s) failed")
 131:         return 1
 132:     print(f"  RESULT: PASS -- zip is ship-ready")
 133:     return 0
 134:

 136: if __name__ == "__main__":

1138: ### Decisions
1139: 
1140: **1) Block J test file** at `tests/integration/test_block_j_ship_gate.py`:

1150:     test: `from sagemaker_agent import CONFIG, BEDROCK_MODELS,
1151:     create_chat_ui` must work in flat-zip layout.

1154:   - `test_real_bedrock_tool_use_round_trip` â€” full tool-use loop:

1156:   - `test_real_bedrock_compact_then_continue` â€” long preamble +
1157:     follow-up call.

1160: **2) Agent module split** (caught by Block J â€” flat-zip import test):
1161: - BEFORE: Agent class lived in `MAIN/agent/__init__.py`. `entry.py`
1162:   imported it via `from agent import Agent`. This failed in the flat
1163:   ship-zip layout because there's no module named `agent` at the zip
1164:   root (only `__init__.py`). Source layout also broke when running
1165:   `python -c "import entry"` directly (worked only under pytest's
1166:   auto sys.path injection).
1167: - AFTER: Agent class moved to `MAIN/agent/agent.py` (a real module).
1168:   `MAIN/agent/__init__.py` rewritten as thin re-export:
1169:   `from .agent import Agent` (relative import â€” resolves to the
1170:   submodule, not the package itself).
1171: 
1172: This dual-layout works in both modes:
1173: - Source layout: tests put `MAIN/agent` on sys.path; `from agent
1174:   import Agent` finds `MAIN/agent/agent.py` directly.
1175: - Flat-zip layout: extracted dir has `agent.py` and `__init__.py`
1176:   side-by-side at root; `from agent import Agent` finds `agent.py`
1177:   directly.
